prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: syngonium went all droopy

so he was fine a few days ago - sitting upright and he gets a few hours from the humidifier everyday (although for 3 days it's been broken but fixed now and back on schedule). i checked the bottom and he's growing out a bit but i only repotted him at the beginning of october and it's winter now so i don't really want to mess with him too much. i thought maybe lack of humidity was the problem but any other suggestions are greatly appreciated 😁😁

it was a freebie from someone so i really had no clue what to do with it ! i suspect i've underwatered then - the room is very hot (and i think the pot is about 2.5-3" so yeah probably dries out too quick) :)

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: underwatering, made worse by dry, hot air.** The roots coming out of the nursery pot's drainage holes look white and firm, which suggests the roots are healthy but the small pot is drying out fast. Syngoniums droop when they're thirsty, and the broken humidifier likely added to the stress.

**Check before watering:** push a finger 2 inches into the soil in the nursery pot. If it's dry, underwatering is confirmed. If it's still damp, hold off and look at the roots for mushiness or a bad smell.

**Fix:**
- Lift the nursery pot out of the cat planter and water it at the sink until water runs out the bottom. Let it drain fully for 10 to 15 minutes.
- Put it back in the cat planter, and pour out any water pooling at the bottom. The planter has no drainage, so standing water can rot roots.
- Water again when the top inch or two of soil is dry, probably every few days in this heat. Don't let it sit in water.
- Keep it away from heaters and vents, and keep the humidifier running. Otherwise it should perk up within a week or two.
